title: Secure Evaluation of Anastomotic Leakage in Robotic Prostatectomy: a prospective, randomized, interventional comparison
summary: During surgery to remove the prostate, the urinary bladder is reconnected to the urethra. To check the tightness of this connection, a standard X-ray examination with liquid contrast medium via the catheter is performed a few days later, exposing the patient to radiation. Alternatively, the tightness can be verified with water directly during surgery. This study investigates whether checking the tightness with water during surgery is just as safe as the later X-ray, allowing the omission of the X-ray without disadvantages for safe catheter removal. The trial includes adult patients undergoing robotic-assisted prostate removal. During surgery, doctors test the connection for leaks using water. If it is tight, a computer-based random system determines whether the patient receives no postoperative X-ray and has the catheter removed routinely on the fourth day, or undergoes the standard X-ray check on the fourth day before catheter removal. Postoperative follow-up assessments are conducted for all patients using questionnaires.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Indication for a planned robot-assisted radical prostatectomy at the University Hospital Würzburg, and presence of written informed consent after being fully informed about study participation
Exclusion criteria:
There are no specific exclusion criteria based on patient characteristics. However, clinical exclusion from randomization into groups A and B occurs if the intraoperative water tightness test of the vesicourethral anastomosis shows a persistent leak
